key_insight: Modeling asynchronous event streams with a dedicated state machine tailored for egocentric, head-mounted cameras yields more accurate and temporally consistent monocular 3D human pose estimates than prior frame-oriented designs.
problem_solved: Existing event-based egocentric 3D pose methods underperform because they treat event data like conventional frames and ignore the stream’s asynchronous, continuous nature, leading to low accuracy and unstable tracking for VR/AR and other real-time applications.
method: Introduce E-3DPSM: an event-driven state machine that segments incoming event streams into semantic/temporal states (e.g., steady, motion, occlusion) and selects state-specific processing paths.
Aggregate asynchronous events into lightweight, state-conditioned representations and feed them to a pose regressor designed for egocentric constraints, preserving millisecond temporal resolution.
Train with temporal-consistency objectives and evaluate on head-mounted event-camera datasets to improve 3D accuracy and temporal stability over prior baselines.
impact: Enables higher-accuracy, low-latency egocentric 3D pose tracking for VR/AR and wearable systems, letting practitioners build more responsive and robust real-time human sensing with energy-efficient event cameras.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the state machine: event input -> state classification -> state-specific feature aggregation -> pose regressor

paper_title: E-3DPSM: A State Machine for Event-Based Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Mayur Deshmukh, Hiroyasu Akada, Helge Rhodin, Christian Theobalt, Vladislav Golyanik
